Class FastqReader

java.lang.Object
global.thalion.ttio.importers.FastqReader
public class FastqReader extends Object
FASTQ importer. Parses FASTQ files into unaligned WrittenGenomicRun instances.

Each four-line record (@name, sequence, +, qualities) becomes one read; SAM unmapped sentinels are written (flags=4, chrom="*", pos=0, mapq=255, cigar="*").

Phred encoding is auto-detected; pass FastqReader(Path,Integer) with an explicit 33 or 64 to override. Internal storage is always Phred+33 ASCII.

Cross-language equivalents: Python ttio.importers.fastq.FastqReader, Objective-C TTIOFastqReader.

  • Field Details

    • PROGRESS_INTERVAL_READS

      public static final int PROGRESS_INTERVAL_READS
      Default emit-every-N cadence for ProgressSink callbacks. Small enough that even small input files get visible updates, large enough that the per-callback overhead stays well below 1% of parse time.

    • detectPhredOffset

      public static int detectPhredOffset(byte[] qualities)
      Heuristic Phred-offset detection over a quality-bytes sample.

      Rule:

      • any byte b < 59 => Phred+33 (Phred+64 starts at b == 64).
      • else if every byte is in [64, 104] => Phred+64.
      • else => Phred+33 (default).

    • read

      public WrittenGenomicRun read(String sampleName, String platform, String referenceUri, Enums.AcquisitionMode acquisitionMode) throws IOException
      Parse the file and return an unaligned WrittenGenomicRun.

      Quality bytes are normalised to Phred+33 internally (verbatim ASCII storage). The detected source offset is recorded on detectedPhredOffset().

      Throws:

    • read

      public WrittenGenomicRun read(String sampleName, String platform, String referenceUri, Enums.AcquisitionMode acquisitionMode, ProgressSink progress) throws IOException
      Parse the file and return an unaligned WrittenGenomicRun, firing progress.onProgress(readsDone, -1L) every PROGRESS_INTERVAL_READS records during the parse phase and a final onProgress(total, total) once the record count is known.

      Total is reported as -1L mid-parse because FASTQ gives no record-count up front; the final fire stamps both done and total with the true count so listeners can switch from indeterminate to determinate display.

      Throws:
      IOException

      1.5.0
